fluff.overview: StarCorps Industries introduced the Manteuffel Attack Tank in 3062 in response to an Armed Forces of the Federated Commonwealth requirement for OmniVehicle designs. Named after a distinguished line of Lyran armor generals, the Manteuffel was StarCorps' first foray into military vehicle production, as the company had previously built only BattleMechs. Despite competing against multiple submissions, the design won the contract decisively, fulfilling all official military requirements. The seventy-ton tracked OmniVehicle combined heavy firepower with enough speed to keep pace with frontline combined-arms formations, earning it a reputation as one of the most capable armored vehicles fielded by the successor states of the former Federated Commonwealth. Its high unit cost and advanced technology base restricted distribution to elite formations, making the Manteuffel a prestige assignment for crews fortunate enough to operate one.
fluff.capabilities:
The Manteuffel's Magna 350 XL fusion engine drives the seventy-ton vehicle to a top speed of 86 km/h, fast enough to keep pace with most medium BattleMech formations. StarSlab/3 ferro-fibrous armor provides eleven and a half tons of protection, enhanced by CASE to contain ammunition explosions. The vehicle dedicates 23.5 tons of pod space to mission-configurable weaponry, with fifteen tons available in the turret and the remainder distributed across hull mounting points.

The Prime configuration pairs a Rotary AC/5 with three extended-range medium lasers, delivering devastating burst damage at medium range. A Guardian ECM suite disrupts enemy electronic warfare systems, while a C3 slave module allows the Manteuffel to share targeting data across a networked lance. This combination makes the Prime a potent force multiplier in coordinated engagements. The XL engine is a significant vulnerability, as penetrating hits to either side can disable the vehicle entirely. The reliance on ammunition-fed weapons in most configurations also limits sustained endurance without resupply, and crews must manage their stores carefully during extended operations.
fluff.deployment: Introduced in 3087 during the early Republic era, the E configuration carries a BattleMech Taser and LB 10-X autocannon in the turret. The Guardian ECM suite is retained from the Prime, but the C3 slave is removed to accommodate the Taser system. A pair of medium lasers and an ER small laser cover the forward arc. The Taser gives the E a unique capability to temporarily disable enemy vehicles and BattleMechs, making it valuable in situations where targets need to be captured intact.
fluff.history:
When the AFFC issued its requirement for OmniVehicle designs in the early 3060s, procurement officials were simultaneously rejecting nearly every OmniMech submission while actively courting manufacturers to produce OmniVehicles instead. The reasoning was financial. Omni-technology equipped vehicles cost approximately the same to produce as their BattleMech equivalents, but the budget allocation for new military vehicles came from a different account than that for BattleMechs. StarCorps Industries, sensing an opportunity, assembled a dedicated military vehicle design team despite having no prior experience in vehicle production. The company produced a working prototype in record time. While the Manteuffel officially won the competition on its merits, persistent rumors suggest that StarCorps leveraged its extensive political connections within the AFFC procurement hierarchy. More than a dozen former AFFC and LAAF officers involved in the selection decision subsequently accepted directorships within StarCorps.

Production began at StarCorps facilities on Crofton, Loburg, and Son Hoa, with all three plants manufacturing the Manteuffel for distribution across both the Lyran Alliance and Federated Suns. The Word of Blake's assault on Son Hoa in April 3074 devastated that facility. Chemical weapons killed the StarCorps Board of Directors during a meeting at the complex, and repeated aerospace and DropShip strikes left the plant inoperable. The loss of Son Hoa reduced Manteuffel production capacity significantly during the Jihad, though the Crofton and Loburg plants continued operations throughout the conflict. Arcturan Arms on Buena joined the production network during the Civil War era, providing additional Lyran Alliance output. The Manteuffel remained in continuous production through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, with StarCorps and Arcturan Arms maintaining active lines to supply both Lyran and Davion forces.
